problems.title: A singleton prompt truncates parallel image batches
claim: Training passes images shaped \((4,1,256,256)\), a degradation prompt \((1,128,128)\), and scenario prompts \((4,64)\) into DataParallel.
analysis: Dimension-zero scattering yields four image/scenario chunks but one degradation chunk. The recursive zip stops at one input, leaving a one-image prediction. For scalar predictor \(f_w(x)=wx\), \(w=1\), four constant images/targets \(0.1,0.2,0.7,0.8\) should have zero loss. Broadcasting the surviving first prediction gives mean absolute loss \(0.35\) and gradient \(-0.075\). Validation passes a scenario vector \((64,)\), which is split into length \(16\) on four destinations, incompatible with the released \(64\)-input linear layer. Single-device operation can avoid this scattering defect.
result: The released multi-device call layout fails its per-example contract. This is a static source/shape finding; no claim of four-physical-GPU execution or false published scores is made.
repair: Before scattering, give every tensor a matching batch axis: degradation \((B,128,128)\), scenario \((B,64)\). Assert equal prediction/target shapes. This restores the identified correspondence, not end-to-end trained performance.

problems.title: The corruptionâ€™s brightness offset differs from the printed formula
problems.source_location: Appendix A.1.1 Eq.(8), PDF p.22; ranges, PDF p.23; dataset.py/create_corrupt.py and Albumentations 1.4.1
claim: The paper specifies \(C(I)=\alpha(I+\beta M)\); the pinned brightness-by-max transform implements \(\alpha I+\beta M\).
analysis: Use valid uint8 intensities \(0,100,200,255\), \(M=255\), and interior hard-range values \(\alpha=0.5,\beta=0.3\). The printed real outputs are \[(38.25,88.25,138.25,165.75)\]; the dependency gives \((76.5,126.5,176.5,204)\). No value saturates, and the real offset difference is \((1-\alpha)\beta M=38.25\). Quantization cannot explain it. Renaming brightness would require correlated parameter changes; at these values the implied paper brightness \(0.6\) exceeds the hard range.
result: The release and printed parameters define different corrupted inputs. Which produced the historical benchmark images is unestablished.
repair: Either document the multiply-then-add generator and ranges, or implement the printed correlated offset. Matching one formula locally does not establish improved restoration or recover historical data.
